intent: Specify the public API of `circular_queue::CircularQueue<T>` instantiated at `T = u32`: `with_capacity`, `len`, `is_empty`, `is_full`, `capacity`, `clear`, `push`, `iter`, `asc_iter` and `into_vec`. In Lean these are `CircularQueue.with_capacity Std.U32 c`, `CircularQueue.len q`, `CircularQueue.is_empty q`, `CircularQueue.is_full q`, `CircularQueue.impl.capacity q`, `CircularQueue.clear q`, `CircularQueue.push q x`, `CircularQueue.iter q`, `CircularQueue.asc_iter q` and `CircularQueue.into_vec q` (`&mut self` is threaded functionally: `clear` returns the new queue, `push` returns the pair (returned value, new queue)); `iter`/`asc_iter` return CoreModels iterator adapters (`Chain`/`Rev` over slice iterators) that can be stepped with the corresponding `Iterator` instances' `next`.

manual_mutants.note: zero-capacity guard removed: pushing into a zero-capacity queue panics
insertion index is not wrapped around: the second lap overwrites out of bounds
push into a full queue returns the new value instead of the overwritten oldest one
clear forgets to reset the insertion index
manual_mutants.before: ok { self with data := v, insertion_index := 0#usize }

manual_mutants.note: asc_iter chains the two halves in the wrong order (only wrong after wrap-around)
into_vec forgets to reverse the lower part
is_full compares against capacity - 1 (reports full one element early)

bug_variants.source: injected (no fixed upstream bug: the issue/PR history of YaLTeR/circular-queue only contains features — zero capacity, is_full, popped values, into_vec)
bug_variants.note: push into a full queue returns the newly pushed value instead of the overwritten oldest one (docs: 'In case an old value is overwritten, it will be returned')
asc_iter chains the two halves in the wrong order: after wrap-around it no longer goes from the oldest to the newest item (and is no longer the reverse of iter)
